newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia LSWR price buoyant on nuclear shut down news.
newsitem.headline: Asia LSWR price buoyant on nuclear shut down news.

text.p: Unexpected nuclear power plant shutdowns in Japan at the height of winter demand is expected to keep low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) prices buoyant despite a cut in imports by other regional consumers, industry sources said on Thursday.

They said prices are likely to remain supported until early next year. Sources said Japan is expected to import more than one million barrels of LSWR in December, up at least 200,000 barrels from November.
Traders said the rise in imports was due to seasonal peak winter demand for heating and power generation amid depleting inventories.
They said problems at two nuclear power plant - Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) and Kansai Electric Power Co - may prompt more LSWR imports to Japan.

TEPCO, Japan's biggest power utility said on Wednesday that it may delay re-starting a nuclear reactor in northern Japan due to ruptures in its pipes which were discovered during routine maintenance checks.
TEPCO said on Thursday, it is unclear if the 460,000 kilowatt nuclear reactor which was down since August, could resume operations in late January as originally planned.

Operations at Kansai Electric's 826,000 kilowatt Takahama nuclear plant had been reduced to 75 percent of capacity to allow the company to check the cause of unusual water levels in the system. Output has been reduced since last Wednesday.
While it remained unclear when the nuclear reactors would start-up, officials said the power reduction could continue for a few more days until investigations are completed.

South Korea has halved is expected December imports to between 500,000-600,000 barrels from the 1.1 million barrels purchased in November. South Korean importers told Reuters that most refineries have started their seasonal switch to low sulphur crude and have raised their production of low sulphur fuel oil at the expense of the usual high sulphur.
As a result South Korean refiners have also cut back on high sulphur fuel oil exports.

India is also expected to lower its import to between 200,000-400,000 barrels, down 200,000 barrels from its imports in November. Traders said India has raised the amount of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) it uses for power generation as LNG is currently cheaper than LSWR.

Inclusive of term exports to Italy at 600,000 barrels, total demand in Asia could rise above 3 million barrels, traders said. Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina, the main exporter of LSWR in Asia, has allocated a total of 3.5 million barrels in December but the supply surplus is easily absorbed by other export markets such as the U.S.
The gradual rise of the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices has opened arbitrage opportunities for LSWR exports to the U.S. with 400,000 barrels already committed to the U.S. in December.
Traders said current alternative burning burning crudes, like Duri and Minas are also expensive and this could spur more buying interest for LSWR
Duri are currently assessed at $21.70 per barrel and Minas at $23.10 against LSWR at $19.00-$19.30 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis.
